text:
kira: Heads up - we're seeing a weird oscillation in GPU queue depth in eu-west-1 over the last ~20m. spikes every ~90s then drops, repeat. latency SLOs are tripping for mosaic-4b and a couple of customer models.

sanjay: saw alerts too, digging into prometheus. is this autoscaler churn or real bursty traffic?

kira: initial hunch: short high-priority bursts are causing preemption + pod churn; autoscaler cooldown and target utilization are too tight so it overshoots then backs off.

marco: plotting pslot occupancy and preempt logs now. here's a short tail from scheduler:```
I0321 15:12:09 scheduler.go:211] preempting pod/generator-req-12 -> assigned gpu-11
I0321 15:12:10 autoscaler.go:134] scaleUp triggered for pool=euw1-mosaic, desired=6 -> 9 (cooldown 30s)
I0321 15:12:19 autoscaler.go:210] scaleDown suggested for pool=euw1-mosaic, desired=9 -> 6 (underutilized)
```

liz: that looks like classic oscillation. also noticed KV cache misses spike when a model moves pods, which causes longer tails and keeps queues hot.

kira: impact: 3 customer routes showing 95th latency >2x for short windows. costwise, we burn extra hours from spinning up nodes repeatedly.

ops-bot: [incident created] incident/INC-20260321-euw-fleet-oscillation by kira - priority P2

sanjay: quick mitigation options: 1) raise autoscaler cooldown to 3m and bump target util to 75% 2) temporarily lower burst-priority for non-prod jobs in euw1 3) enable admission control to cap concurrent requests per model to avoid pslot hogging

marco: agree. also we can enable sticky-scheduling for heavy models so their KV cache stays warm on crash/reassigns for a bit (ttl 5m). less cold-start churn.

kira: doing 1 and 2 now. I'll patch autoscaler config in staging then roll to euw1. sanjay, can you flip non-prod burst down?

sanjay: on it. turning down burst to 20% for pools: euw1-dev, euw1-ci. patching admission control rule to limit concurrency for model "mosaic-4b" to 12 requests concurrently as emergency throttle.

liz: I'll start a small canary of sticky-scheduling for mosaic-4b with ttl=300s. will watch KV cache hit rate.

marco: after the autoscaler patch applied, I see scale events calm down. queue depth now shows a dampened waveform instead of full swings.

kira: nice. ops-bot, update the incident with mitigations and assign follow-ups. we need an RCA: why were cooldowns set so low and why adm-control defaults allowed high concurrency for mosaic-4b?

ops-bot: [incident updated] mitigations: raised autoscaler cooldown to 180s, decreased non-prod burst by 80%, applied emergency concurrency cap for mosaic-4b, enabled sticky-scheduling canary. assigned to: sanjay, marco, liz.

sanjay: immediate patch worked. next steps: revamp autoscaler heuristics to include p99 queue growth as a signal, not just avg utilization. also add a hysteresis window so we don't oscillate on short bursts.

marco: follow-up item: implement per-model admission policy that auto-lowers concurrency for models with high cold-start cost. opening a PR to add model annotation for cold-start-weight.

liz: monitoring tasks: 1) add KV cache hit rate panel per-model 2) add queue-oscillation alert (pattern detection of >3 cycles in 5m) 3) daily runbook updates.

kira: thanks all. I'll keep incident open until next = 4h with green metrics. good job on fast mitigation. :thumbsup:

sanjay: one more note — cost delta during the 20m oscillation was ~+15% in euw1. will surface in cost report.

marco: logging note: saved preempt IDs and logs to /var/ops/incidents/1778889999 for RCA.

liz: canary looks good, KV hit rate up ~35% after sticky scheduling. queue depth normalized.

kira: closing loop: action owners - sanjay autoscaler heuristics, marco admission PR, liz monitoring panels. check-ins EOD.

ops-bot: [incident status] monitoring - stable. will auto-close in 4h if unchanged.
